findings.confidence: HIGH for this saved-data computation; independent broad performance unestablished
findings.source: Frozen-beat pilot revision 2, results and verification, 2026-10-27.

findings.title: Independent-looking strata must not be overstated
findings.detail: All 151 retained: 100 exact training-partition cases; 21 exact publisher-validation cases; 18 related-comp solos; 12 unresolved. In the 21 validation-partition cases, direct is 1/21 = 4.76% and previous preprocessing 7/21 = 33.33%, with no missing. Publisher validation and shared performer/session families are not untouched independent confirmation.
findings.evidence_type: Pinned original publisher splits, checkpoint metadata and saved-result subgroup audit
findings.confidence: HIGH for partition mapping and counts; LOW for broad generalization
findings.source: Publisher v1.0 single split and frozen-beat pilot, 2026-10-27.

findings.title: Subgroup regressions and DP safety failures retained
findings.detail: Combined direct failures: drums 5/115 = 4.35%; guitar 8/36 = 22.22%; guitar solos 6/18 = 33.33%. All three new direct regressions versus preprocessing are solos. Five related-validation solos worsen from 1/5 to 3/5; unresolved cases remain 4/12 combined failures. DP fabricates about 300 BPM on quiet/non-rhythmic controls, so no production promotion.
findings.evidence_type: Actual per-case comparisons, provenance breakdown and retained negative controls
findings.confidence: HIGH for these recorded inputs; no universal reliability claim
findings.source: Frozen-beat pilot case changes, controls and outcome closure, 2026-10-27.

findings.title: Historical preprocessing pilot: incidence rescoring
findings.detail: At an 8% BPM tolerance: original mean 41.06% (62/151); original median 41.72% (63/151); percussive mean 41.06% (62/151); percussive median 39.07% (59/151); harmonic median 49.01% (74/151). No missing predictions. Severe deviations above 50%: baseline and percussive median both 17.88% (27/151). Each offending recording counts once, regardless of error size.
findings.evidence_type: Owner-directed post-hoc incidence reanalysis of unchanged pilot outputs
findings.confidence: HIGH for saved-data arithmetic; no independent musical/generalization validation
findings.source: Threshold-incidence policy and rescoring,2026-10-27; direct deterministic computation. Historical mean-error findings below are secondary, not failure rates.

findings.title: Existing five preprocessing outputs have a fixed-pool limit
findings.detail: Even reference-informed perfect selection among those exact five outputs leaves 48/151 = 31.79% above the 8% tempo-error tolerance. This is not a bound on all preprocessing or the expanded candidate bank. Of the current 59 failures, 29 are mathematically half/double-compatible with reference BPM; actual reference-blind correction remains unproved.
findings.evidence_type: Post-hoc fixed saved-output diagnostic; not a deployable oracle
findings.confidence: HIGH for fixed-data arithmetic; LOW for achievable benefit
findings.source: Below30%headroom audit,2026-10-27.

findings.title: Candidate availability is not selection performance
findings.detail: The earlier expanded bank contains a candidate within 8% for 149/151 recordings, but its reference-informed 1.32% oracle failure is NOT model performance. Actual incidence: linear 48.34%; MLP 47.68–49.01%. Fresh papers and benchmark trade-offs favor testing stronger frozen rhythm evidence before assuming decoder-only rescue.
findings.evidence_type: All saved selector seeds rescored; targeted academic/benchmark synthesis
findings.confidence: HIGH for saved-output arithmetic; MEDIUM for research priority, no forecast
findings.source: Selector incidence crosscheck and literature review,2026-10-27; eventF1scores are not recording-level8%failure rates.

findings.title: Pulse-level mistakes dominate a large share of retained drum error
findings.detail: Using the predeclared descriptive 4% reference-relative half/double-nearness rule, 22 of 115 drum records account for 64.49% of summed exact relative error. The corresponding guitar values are 3 of 78 and 14.32%. This is retained-development arithmetic, not a new model gain or proof of perceptual correctness.
findings.evidence_type: Executed retained-record reanalysis
findings.confidence: HIGH for the retained arithmetic; generalization unestablished
findings.source: diagnosis/RESULTS.md and diagnosis.json, 2026-10-24; internal development evidence

findings.title: The frozen baseline reproduces a numerical half-rate case
findings.detail: On a synthetic 180-pulse-per-minute control, the unchanged estimator returns 89.1 BPM. Silence, DC and the tested sustained tone return unavailable BPM. These controls establish numerical behavior only, not musical accuracy.
findings.evidence_type: Fresh rhythm-only CPU execution
findings.confidence: HIGH for this pinned execution only
findings.source: baseline/baseline-results.json, 2026-10-24; deterministic execution artifact

findings.title: Reference availability, not file availability, is the immediate bottleneck
findings.detail: The scoped local inventory found 1,241 media files and 746 existing benchmark audio memberships. Repeated/inspected material, isolated notes, uncertain composition identity and rights/overlap gaps mean zero sources are yet demonstrated eligible for new independent confirmation. This does not mean every local recording is unusable.
findings.evidence_type: Executed filesystem/manifest and retained-rights audit
findings.confidence: HIGH for scoped counts and documented eligibility status; broader availability unknown
findings.source: references/local_inventory.json and README.md, 2026-10-24; internal inventory

findings.title: A close 2026 architecture baseline changes the novelty boundary
findings.detail: Explore This! already learns a tatum grid and joint beat/downbeat metrical interpretations. Joint pulse/grid modeling alone is therefore not a sufficient novelty claim. Its reported limitations motivate candidates, but no local performance claim is replicated. The primary PDF and original reproduction-code commit were inspected.
findings.evidence_type: Primary academic paper, official conference page and released source
findings.confidence: HIGH on verified existence/overlap; local transfer unverified
findings.source: Kihlborg, Holzapfel and Schlüter, Explore This! (ISMIR 2026); https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.14817 and https://github.com/CPJKU/explore_this

findings.title: Small learned selectors failed cross-corpus transfer
findings.detail: Pooled exact metadata BPM mean error increased from 25.017% frozen to 37.187% linear and 35.413–37.446% MLP. Above-50% error cases increased from 27/151 to 48/151 linear and 49–52/151 MLP. Lower medians for some arms did not compensate for worse tails. No learned checkpoint is promoted.
findings.evidence_type: Actual training on opposite-corpus development folds; verified saved predictions
findings.confidence: HIGH for this bounded numerical result; broad musical generalization unestablished
findings.source: local selector pilot results, verification and independent technical closure, 2026-10-27; direct execution and technical review

findings.title: Candidate support is not successful selection
findings.detail: A reference-informed candidate oracle has 1.066% mean error; candidates within 8% metadata BPM exist for 36/36 guitar and 113/115 drum recordings. This is a diagnostic ceiling, not an achieved model gain or evidence of perceptually correct musical pulse.
findings.evidence_type: Reference-informed diagnostic over the frozen extracted candidate bank
findings.confidence: HIGH for the arithmetic only; no achieved improvement
findings.source: local selector pilot candidate-support and oracle records, 2026-10-27; internal diagnostic

findings.detail: Mean exact metadata BPM error: original25.0171%, raw median24.7568%, percussive mean24.7402%, percussive median24.2945%, harmonic median30.5686%. Lowest observed mean arm improves6/worsens5/unchanged140; within8%89->92, severe errors27->27. Original median has fewer severe errors25. No universal cleanup or production recommendation.

findings.confidence: HIGH for these inspected numerical outputs; musical/generalization benefit unverified
findings.source: Preprocessing pilot results, verification and independent outcome review,2026-10-27; direct execution and read-only review.

findings.title: Effects differ by category; pulse ambiguity survives
findings.detail: Percussive+median mean error guitar20.5457->20.1876%, drums26.4168->25.5801%; three extra within8% cases are drums. Guitar accompaniment and >90s recordings are unchanged for this arm. All32category groups retained privately. The180-pulse numerical control still returns89.1BPM on original/percussive views.

findings.confidence: HIGH for scoped arithmetic; no causal or perceptual claim

limits: Coarse19 changes reporting specificity and raises severe11→14; reject promotion despite62/292. Administrative publication budget extension does not authorize new model inference.

Deployed checkpoints, not second-by-second monitoring. Refresh after a milestone deployment.
Synthetic controls test numerical behavior, not musical correctness.
Old diagnostic recordings are not fresh confirmation material.
CLPR remains the flagship. This is a proposed task-specific recognizer-qualification lane; rhythm/meter accuracy does not validate register or note-density constructs.

This local pilot uses only guitar/drum corpora and weak global BPM labels; it cannot satisfy the owner’s final-run diversity requirement. The final diverse acquisition/training run is not started or budgeted.

Scoring update: use above-tolerance incidence as the current headline; historical mean relative error is not the percentage of recordings that failed. The8%threshold is specific to this tempo benchmark, not a universal tolerance for chords/instruments/beat timing.

The frozen pilot was research-only at its original dated milestone; later owner-authorized development integrated the direct global-tempo method. No new training or hosted model release occurred in this package.
Chord matched seconds are retained approved-score observations; the fresh stdlib partition is not an independent mir_eval reproduction or expert musical annotation.
No severe/missing cases are concealed by aggregate success; the weak solo and unresolved tempo subsets remain open.
A model paper, its repository and its checkpoint mirror are one evidence lineage, not independent performance replications.

The later fresh standard-score replay supersedes only the earlier inability to replay. It does not reconstruct the historical scoring process or turn the inspected developmental guitar corpus into independent musical validation.

Recording-level metadata review is not legal clearance. Only humans can supply independent audible reference judgments here; future reference rights/consent and all confirmatory tolerances remain unresolved. The response checker cannot verify human independence or musical truth.

Current storage authorization (31 October): justified storage and demonstrably disposable cleanup are allowed; alert only below 15 GB free. Required source/data/checkpoints/evidence are retained. Earlier dated 30 GiB pauses are historical.

The prior recording-clearance commit was pushed but failed its live publication gate; last verified prior five-file checkpoint remained the older chord-readiness page. Current publication is only established by exact deployment/live read-back, never by a push.

Primary failure means at least one disagreement on an observed reference class; unknown/unannotated classes are never negatives. Three reference-unscorable recordings remain in current295-input inference accounting (292scorable); the historical49-input diagnostic had two.
PaSST publisher TEST served validation/checkpoint selection. New local artist groups do not imply independence from model selection, compositions or pretrained exposure.

The descriptive artist-cluster95% interval for candidate-minus-baseline failure incidence spans -25.00 to +2.44 percentage points; it includes no difference. No population-level improvement is established.

Historical global comparator rescored only eleven existing singleton names. The current experimental arm additionally suppresses eight coarse/multimember classes, without boosting exact subtypes or inventing rows. Vocal/world vocabulary stays unchanged; no production adoption.

These results concern ten-second clips. The prepared local integration must fall back on longer inputs; a first-window score must not be assigned to an entire song. Full-track pooling and section audibility remain separate experiments.
Genres and marked/not-marked instrumental are overlapping track metadata, not verified excerpt vocal/solo/live/studio conditions. Broad independent final audio-condition coverage remains open.

Source licence and conditional author weight permission do not establish commercial/hosted/redistribution clearance. No paid annotation/data/compute service was used; existing assistant billing and electricity are excluded.
The native PaSST0.50 coarse-head diagnostic is not the hybrid or a deployable fine-instrument mapping. Sigmoid scores are not calibrated presence probabilities.
